subject: Finalize evaluation acceptance checklist & go/no-go tasks
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novamed.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP + acceptance checkpoints for the Novamed evaluation

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our discussion I pulled together a compact mutual action plan with the concrete acceptance checks that will be used to decide go/no-go at the end of the three-week evaluation. I attached a working spreadsheet (redwood-map-v2.xlsx) and a short markdown doc that lists the acceptance test cases.

High-level asks from your side:
- Confirm the two primary success metrics (inference latency at 95th pct, and classification concordance at sample-level).
- Confirm who on Novamed will own the smoke validations (we suggested Tom as the technical contact).
- Sign off on the final rollback triggers (we propose automatic fallback to the lightweight quantized model if token error rate > 0.8% for three consecutive runs).

Key timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): MAP agreed, infra access completed, seed dataset shared.
- Week 1: Baseline runs, KV-cache smoke tests, latency profiling.
- Week 2: Edge-case concordance tests and throughput ramp.
- Week 3: Acceptance run, close meeting and sign-off.

Exit gates (examples in the sheet):
- Pass: 95th pct latency <= 220ms on our test harness AND concordance >= 92% on the labeled sample set.
- Fail: Concordance < 88% OR sustained error rate spikes after retry policy.

Next steps: If you can confirm the owners and give a quick thumbs up on the acceptance thresholds today or tomorrow, Marissa and I will lock the test vectors and schedule the first baseline run.

Thanks —
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132

Attachments: redwood-map-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), acceptance-tests-v1.md (markdown)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novamed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 12:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + acceptance checkpoints for the Novamed evaluation

Logan —

Thanks, this looks good and much clearer than our previous plans. Quick answers from our side:
- We confirm the two primary success metrics. Can we change the latency SLO to 200ms at 95th for the patient-queue profile? That target is tight but would be ideal.
- Tom will own the smoke validations and will coordinate infra access. He copied him above.
- Rollback triggers look reasonable — one question: can you add a manual review step before we flip to fallback quantized model? Our clinical QA wants a human-in-the-loop confirmation for any automatic model switch.

We should be able to sign the MAP by end of day tomorrow after Tom completes the infra checklist.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Novamed
Elena.Park@novamed.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novamed.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 08:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + acceptance checkpoints for the Novamed evaluation

Appreciate the quick reply, Elena —

We can do 200ms at 95th for the patient-queue profile as a stretch goal. For go/no-go we recommend keeping 220ms as the control threshold and call 200ms a stretch milestone tied to a pricing uplift conversation (we'll note that in the MAP).

Regarding the manual review before fallback: agreed. We'll add a two-step flow:
1) automated detection of a sustained token error spike (our system flags it),
2) Novamed clinical QA acknowledges within a 30-minute window, otherwise we hold on rollback and route requests to the hosted safe-path model (no automatic quantized switch).

I've updated the acceptance-tests-v1.md with the concrete test cases (attached) and added a short column to the spreadsheet linking each test to an evidence artifact (logs, sample responses, trace ids). Also attached the kv-cache smoke results summary from our internal runs (kv-cache-smoke-results.pdf) so Tom can validate the harness.

Marissa, Soojin — can you confirm that the evidence collection steps in sheet tab "Evidence" match our tracing instrumentation (trace id, token-level sampling, cost-per-token snapshot)? We want to avoid any mismatch when Novamed hands over traces.

Tom — can you share the infra checklist items you still need from us? Linking them in HubSpot would be helpful.

If we get a sign-off tomorrow, we can start baseline runs Monday morning (your timezone).

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance-tests-v1.md, kv-cache-smoke-results.pdf
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@novamed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + acceptance checkpoints for the Novamed evaluation

All — quick update from infra:
- I completed the network allowlist and provided service account keys to your infra@ address.
- I verified the KV-cache harness ran against our sample corpus; attached are two sample trace ids we used for the run (see HubSpot note).
- We accept the evidence requirements as described. One minor ask: can you add a short checklist item that documents tokenization parity for our preprocessing pipeline? We got a mismatch once during an internal test and want to avoid surprises.

Elena — Tom to own the sign-off on infra; I'm good for the MAP sign-off as soon as we see the tokenization parity item. Logan — please append that to the Evidence tab and I will tick the infra checklist in HubSpot.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior Engineering Manager, Novamed
